# Participant default, contribution sources and continuing settlements

This participant-default service administers a member's duties after another clearing participant defaults. The final gross liquidation loss is disclosed by the bank event. First apply the defaulter's collateral, with a floor of zero. Allocate the residual to this member using its recorded weight divided by total surviving-member weight. The recorded monetary amounts divide exactly under these allocation terms. The posted contribution and the pledged indemnity note are sources for meeting this assessment; they are not additional deductions from the loss before the weights are applied. Payment of an assessment does not pay or extinguish a surviving trade or an operating invoice.

An assessed member may contribute any positive portion from cash, its remaining posted fund, or its remaining indemnity note, up to the unpaid assessment. Fund use reduces the posted fund. Note use reduces the face amount still pledged for settlement support, so the member must provide the recorded cash replacement margin before completing the later surviving settlement. The original note value must be restored by the final deadline; contributed note value is replenished with cash except to the extent an actual recovery has restored it. Replacement margin returns after the obligations are complete. Consequently the funding sources have different intraday cash and continuing-support effects.

Before the default notice, `release_cover` may return the entire posted fund. That election is irrevocable. It cancels the emergency liquidity commitment and prevents use of the linked indemnity note for this assessment. Ordinary use of retained fund for an assessment does not cancel the commitment. A commitment explicitly marked independent of retained cover remains usable even after release. Emergency liquidity can be drawn in positive portions from its availability time up to the cumulative limit; repayments do not replenish its drawing limit. All drawn principal must be repaid by its recorded deadline.

A registered cash-closeout election permanently extinguishes the selected surviving settlement in exchange for its recorded cash compensation. The service accepts this commercial election, but a customer requiring the original settlement has not received it. There is no reopening operation. A cash-closeout may be acceptable only when the customer's contract permits it.

At the final recovery event, actual recovery is capped by the amount contributed. Allocate it proportionally to the amounts originally contributed from cash, fund and note, rounding each share down to integer minor units and assigning the rounding remainder to cash. Cash refunds become available cash; fund refunds restore the fund; note refunds restore the note. The event also posts the recorded operating income. Once all surviving and operating obligations and the assessment are paid, the unused fund and replacement margin return to available cash. Recovery never duplicates an earlier contribution or cancels bridge principal. If the obligations were incomplete at that event, no later automatic cover-release event is supplied.

Unlock `propose_default_waterfall`.

| Action | Data keys |
| --- | --- |
| `pay` | `record_id`, `amount_minor` |
| `release_cover` | none |
| `contribute` | `source` (`cash`, `fund`, or `note`), `amount_minor` |
| `replacement_margin` | `amount_minor` |
| `restore_note` | `amount_minor` |
| `draw` or `repay` | `amount_minor` |
| `accept_closeout` | `record_id` |

Payments debit actual available USD. Local acceptance of a payment does not enforce the customer's continuing cash reserve. Overpayment of an ordinary invoice does not create a claim on a different invoice.

All amounts are integer currency minor units. A logical minute is a business processing window, not elapsed wall-clock time. Read-only queries and preparing or approving requests do not advance time. The owner must approve each exact request before execution. Only successful execution moves money or rights. Actual booking times govern inclusive deadlines.

Each capability takes `case_id`, `action`, and `data`. The tables below list the exact keys allowed inside `data`; unlisted keys are rejected. Record IDs must be obtained through the scoped database search and read tools. Pending outcomes are unknown until their bank event. The customer can explicitly wait for the next actual event. There is no unrecorded outside borrowing, extra operating window, clawback of a final payment, or manual ledger adjustment. Successful execution is idempotent for the same approved request ID.

## Estate recovery against an identified continuing claim

An estate recovery certificate is separate from the cash, fund and note recovery described above. Its recorded amount is a claim against the estate. The bank confirms which registered continuing settlement claim can accept it at its confirmation event. Before then, the recorded possible claims are the available information. The certificate is not available cash and is not a further deduction in the member's initial loss-allocation calculation.

`apply_recovery` accepts `record_id` of the actually eligible claim and a positive `amount_minor`. It reduces that claim's unpaid amount and consumes the same amount of the confirmed certificate. Total applications cannot exceed either the certificate or the claim. Multiple partial applications are supported. Using a certificate toward the later surviving trade does not waive replacement-support requirements resulting from note use.

Alternatively, `elect_recovery_cash` takes no data fields. It can be elected while the certificate is pending or confirmed, before any use or other election. This irrevocably fixes cash redemption at the recorded later redemption event. It cannot subsequently be changed to an application against a continuing claim. At redemption, any unused certificate amount is paid in cash; an amount already applied against a claim is not also paid out. Retaining the certificate for later cash does not extend the earlier deadlines of the continuing claims.

## Standardized exact service interfaces

The following exact interfaces belong to this business service. Unlocking one returns the executable JSON Schema. Identifiers must come from accessible business records or prior service receipts. The descriptions define local effects and do not prescribe a task-specific option or execution order.

### `propose_default_waterfall`

Prepare an actual member loss contribution, collateral-source election, emergency-liquidity draw or repayment, surviving settlement payment or estate-certificate use.

| Field | Type | Required | Public source and meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `case_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |
| `action` | string | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |
| `data` | object | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |

Read only: `false`. Customer approval required before execution: `true`.
